title: How Are Thy Glories Here Display'd
description: How Are Thy Glories Here Display'd in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book III, prepared for the Lord's Supper, hymn 25, headed “Divine glories, and our graces”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How are thy glo-ries here dis-play'd, Great God, how bright they shine, While at thy word we break the bread, And pour the flow-ing wine!

lines: How are thy glories here display'd,
Great God, how bright they shine,
While at thy word we break the bread,
Here saving mercy spreads her hands
Thy saints attend with every grace
And love appears with cheerful face,
Our hope in waiting posture sits,
Zeal and revenge perform their part,
Dear Saviour, change our faith to sight,
Then shall our souls be all delight,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
